title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-19
content:
2024-11-08 - scratchpad / todo (gpu ops)

Top priorities:
- Finish capacity plan for q4 dedicated pools (nvlink-optimized configs) — need numbers from profiler run (see notes).
- Fix intermittent pod OOMs in batcher-prod (observed 11/06 evening).
- Follow up with network team on MTU mismatch in us-west-2 spot cluster.

Morning checklist:
- Check overnight profiler run: /s3/infra/profiler/runs/2024-11-07-3 -> got 1800 samples. Need to extract mean tail-latency per sequence-length bin.
- Verify disk space on model cache nodes (cache-01..04) > 120GB free.
- Slack: ping @Priya for canary rollout window.

Current tasks (short):
1) Capacity planning (high)
   - Target: ensure Dedicated gpu-pool-4 can sustain 350 rps of 8k-sequence generation at p95 < 2200ms.
   - Action: run loadtest with model=redwood-13b-8k-quant, batch_size=8, concurrency=40.
   - Note: try enabling continuous-batching=on and kv-cache-prefix=true.
2) Investigate pod OOMs (medium-high)
   - Error: oom_kill on batcher-worker-*. Logs show repeated growth at step 42. Might be memory leak in attention cache eviction path.
   - Quick repro: run stress test locally with long sequences (~12k) and watch heap.
   - Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789 (memory-fix WIP).
3) Network MTU issue (medium)
   - Symptom: dropped packets on large-grpc streams between us-west-2 cache nodes and gpu-hosts.
   - Possible cause: MTU mismatched on ENIs after node recycle.
   - Temporary mitigation: reduce grpc keepalive window, enable retry/backoff.
   - Follow-up: schedule downtime with infra-network (PLAT-482).
4) Quick infra housekeeping (low)
   - Recreate kube-secret for nvprof (expires 2024-11-10).
   - Add runbook note for emergency model-fallback (doc link: confluence/infra/model-fallback).

Notes from profiler run:
- Batch sizes peaked at 12 during busy windows; recommends capping to 8 for redwood-13b-8k quantized.
- KV cache hits ~42% for chat workloads; we can tune prefix caching policy to improve.
- Observed slight thrash when autoscaler tries to scale down; consider cooldown + metric smoothing.

Commands / quick snippets:
- tail logs: kubectl -n prod logs -l app=batcher-worker --since=2h --tail=200
- run loadtest: ./tools/loadtest --model redwood-13b-8k-quant --concurrency 40 --batch 8 --duration 10m --out results/q4-capacity-11-08.json
- check disk: ssh cache-01 df -h /model-cache

Open questions / TODOs to clarify:
- Do we want to enable cross-node NVLink pooling for Dedicated customers? (requires infra change + quota)
- What's the rollback plan if memory-fix PR causes perf regression? Add canary with 10% traffic and perf guard rails.

Meeting notes (11/07 quick):
- With @Priya and @Tom: agree to try batch cap=8 for next 48hrs.
- Network will validate MTU across us-west-2 EFA pool by Friday (2024-11-10).

Reminders / personal:
- Create follow-up ticket summarizing profiler findings and attach sample traces (INFRA-912).
- Update personal checklist: look into improved alerting for kv-cache-miss-rate > 30% (pager today at 9:30am was noisy).

Scratch ideas (brainstorm):
- Add heuristic to scheduler to favor nodes with warm model-cache to reduce cold-start I/O peaks.
- Consider small local redis pool on gpu-hosts for prefix cache seeding.

Unresolved:
- Still seeing two OOMs since 11/06; need to repro in staging with same workload.

If stuck:
- Roll back batcher-worker image to v2024-10-30 (known-good) and observe for 2 hours; if stable, debug memory-fix PR on side branch.

Links / refs:
- Profiler results path: s3://redwood-infra/profiler/2024-11-07-3
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-912

Notes to self: keep this doc light — transfer persistent runbook items to confluence and ticket tracker.

-- Ethan
